candidates.bio: Ejji Smith is a Toronto artist and collaborator working across hip-hop and R&B. Sony Music Canada has identified Smith among the Torontonian artists featured on TOBi's Toronto Remix of Dollas and Cents, placing the artist within the city's contemporary rap and soul community. Northern Dial carries Ejji Smith as part of its Toronto music catalogue.
Vancouver singer-songwriter EKKSTACY makes moody Canadian indie rock and post-punk that mixes new-wave textures, punk energy and emotionally direct songwriting.
Bowmanville, Ontario group Eleven Past One was a Canadian pop band best known for the radio single The World Is Ours and melodic, harmony-driven pop-rock.
Vancouver Island-raised Canadian singer-songwriter and pianist Elysia Biro blends classical technique, jazz improvisation and contemporary pop songwriting in a polished, piano-led sound.

Eman Alali is an Iranian and Iraqi-Saudi artist with Canadian roots whose indie-pop songwriting was shaped in part by growing up in Cornwall, Ontario. Her work explores identity, belonging and emotionally detailed pop songwriting, and she has since continued her career internationally. Northern Dial carries Eman Alali as part of its Canadian independent pop catalogue.
South Sudanese-Canadian rapper, author and activist Emmanuel Jal is based in Toronto and uses hip-hop, storytelling and humanitarian work to address war, resilience and peacebuilding.

Endangered Species is a Canadian old-school hip-hop duo from Calgary, Alberta, made up of Infinite P and Nohow. The group recorded its underground album Intangible in a home studio and saw the project spread from Calgary across Canada and into international underground rap circles. Northern Dial carries Endangered Species as part of its archival Western Canadian hip-hop catalogue.
Algerian-born, Montréal-raised rapper Enima is a prominent figure in Québec hip-hop whose music connects Montréal street rap with francophone influences from Canada and France.

Eric Kane is an Edmonton singer-songwriter and former frontman of Kane Incognito whose music blends folk, rock and emotionally direct pop songwriting. After beginning as a drummer, he moved to the microphone and developed a solo career built around personal storytelling, grief, resilience and growth. Northern Dial carries Eric Kane as part of its contemporary Western Canadian singer-songwriter catalogue.

Dartmouth singer-songwriter Eric Stephen Martin is a Nova Scotia indie-rock artist and co-founder of Three First Names Records. His solo work includes the rock album Paper Chains, which won Rock Recording of the Year at the 2025 Music Nova Scotia Awards.

Erin B is a Jamaica-born, Toronto-based singer and artist whose music moves between dancehall, R&B and hip-hop. After settling in Toronto, she became part of the city's independent contemporary music scene through solo work and collaborations. Northern Dial carries Erin B as part of its Toronto R&B and Caribbean-influenced catalogue.

Es, born Eseme Elango, is a Mississauga hip-hop MC whose work is rooted in golden-era boom-bap and the Gillbreathing family alongside Elaquent, Solar-C and Mathematik. He has released a long-running independent catalogue through projects including Feud For Thought, We Are Only Getting Older and You Want A Piece Of Me?. His appearance on Elaquent's Carnival with Mathematik and Solar-C is his Northern Dial library credit.

Toronto singer-songwriter Esthero emerged in the late 1990s with a sound that sat between trip-hop, R&B, jazz and alternative pop at a moment when those scenes were only beginning to overlap in the Canadian mainstream. Working initially with producer Doc McKinney, she released the debut album Breath from Another in 1998. Its atmospheric production, live instrumentation and songs such as "Heaven Sent" and the title track gave Esthero an identity distinct from the era's more rigidly separated rock, dance and R&B formats. The album was nominated for Best Alternative Album at the 1999 JUNO Awards and became a cult touchstone for listeners drawn to adventurous late-1990s pop production.

A long gap followed before Esthero returned with the 2005 EP We R in Need of a Musical Revolution! and the album Wikked Lil' Grrrls. By then her music had widened further, incorporating orchestral pop, hip-hop collaborations and cabaret-inflected songwriting rather than attempting to reproduce the mood of her debut. Between her own releases, she remained active through soundtrack work and collaborations, including recordings with artists from Black Eyed Peas and Goodie Mob to Saul Williams. That flexibility helped establish her as a vocalist and writer whose career reached beyond the conventional album cycle.

Esthero matters in Canadian music because Breath from Another anticipated a kind of genre-fluid Toronto pop that would become much more common in the following decade. Her catalogue never followed a straightforward commercial arc, but its combination of electronic production, soul phrasing and alternative songwriting made her an important bridge between underground club and trip-hop culture and a broader Canadian pop audience. The later work reinforces that reputation: Esthero has treated stylistic freedom, rather than consistency of format, as the through-line of her career.

Every Last Chance is a Canadian pop and electronic studio project built around rhythmic, radio-ready songwriting and rotating featured vocalists. The project broke through in the mid-2010s with singles including Spotlight featuring Marissa Dattoli and Roll the Credits, then released its self-titled debut EP in 2016.

FABjustfab is a Montreal-based rapper, beatboxer, musician and producer, and a co-founder of alternative hip-hop group Random Recipe. Her solo work blends hip-hop, funk, R&B and Latin influences, building on years of international touring and festival appearances. Northern Dial carries FABjustfab as part of Quebec's contemporary independent hip-hop scene.
Montréal-born French-Canadian singer Face-T blends reggae, dancehall and electronic music, drawing on childhood years in Jamaica and collaborations across Québec's bass-music scene.
Mississauga-based rapper Fame Holiday is a Canadian hip-hop artist known for melodic hooks, independent releases and storytelling rooted in life outside Toronto's downtown core.
Montréal-born rapper and broadcaster Famous, born Ashton Bishop, is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose debut EP I Rap Now earned a Juno Award nomination before he expanded his career internationally.
Brandon, Manitoba group Farm Fresh was a pioneering Canadian independent hip-hop trio formed by Mcenroe, Pip Skid and DJ Hunnicutt and closely tied to the Peanuts & Corn label.

Fax4 is a Halifax hip-hop crew made up of Spesh K, Quake Matthews, Boy-Ill and Markit. Active in Nova Scotia's mid-2000s rap scene, the group released the 2006 album Inklined and became part of the broader East Coast Canadian underground alongside artists including Classified and Mic Boyd.
Toronto rapper FB emerged from the city's northwest hip-hop scene alongside Robin Banks, Pressa and GD, appearing on the 2015 collaboration "Wass Gang" and Robin Banks' 2016 single "Priceless."

Fidelina is a Canadian R&B and pop singer-songwriter whose music centres soulful vocals and intimate contemporary production. She has been highlighted among emerging Canadian musicians and has released independent singles including I Don't Wanna and When It Rains. Northern Dial carries Fidelina as part of its emerging Canadian R&B catalogue.
Vancouver-area twin sisters Alanna and Brianne Finn-Morris perform as Fionn, a Canadian indie-pop duo whose harmony-rich songwriting has evolved from folk-pop toward alternative rock.
Panamanian-Canadian singer, songwriter and producer Fito Blanko is a Mississauga-rooted tropical urban artist whose music combines reggaeton, dancehall and North American pop and hip-hop influences.
Québec composer Mathieu David Gagnon's project Flore Laurentienne creates instrumental orchestral and electronic music inspired by nature, landscape and the St. Lawrence region.

Francesco Antonio is a Toronto-born actor, recording artist, writer and director whose music career developed alongside his film and television work. After meeting Canadian reggae artist Snow in a Toronto studio, he joined Snow's DKO Music Group and became part of the label's emerging artist roster. His appearance on Snow's 2020 single Together with William Dinero and Balam Kiel is his Northern Dial library credit.

Frankenstein is the stage name of Toronto rapper, producer and remixer Frank Fallico, a key figure in Canada's mid-1990s underground hip-hop scene. He founded the Knowledge of Self label, earned consecutive Juno nominations for The Rain Is Gone and UV and produced work for artists including Choclair and Maestro Fresh Wes.
Toronto rapper Frankie Payne is a veteran of the city's underground hip-hop scene and a member of the Freedom Writers collective, known for reflective lyricism rooted in his Jane-Finch community.

FREAKEY! is a Montréal producer and artist from the Saint-Léonard and Repentigny areas whose futuristic hip-hop production has reached artists in Canada, the United States and Europe. Raised in a Haitian family in Montréal, he has produced for artists including Don Toliver, Hamza, KILLY and Lost while developing his own solo catalogue. His 2020 collaboration EUPHORIA with Toronto producer WondaGurl is his Northern Dial library credit.

Fredy V, born Fredy Varre, is a Washington, D.C.-born singer, composer and multi-instrumentalist whose career has been rooted in Montréal since moving there to study music at McGill. He co-founded the Kalmunity Vibe Collective, fronted the Boogie Wonder Band and later led The Foundation, blending funk, R&B, Afrobeats and hip-hop. DIDN'T CHA KNOW, NO TRIBE NO I and PHO THE VIBE from Fredy V & The Foundation's 2025 album account for his three Northern Dial library credits.

Freq Motif is a Toronto electronic duo formed in 2020 by two Canadian producers. Their music mixes world, dance and Latin influences with pop-minded production, with releases including Hot, Sirena and Nice To Meet Ya. Northern Dial carries Freq Motif as part of Toronto's contemporary electronic scene.

Fresco Rhodes, also known as Finesse, is a Toronto-based Canadian producer, composer, keyboardist and mix engineer. His production work spans hip-hop, R&B and pop, including collaborations with EverythingOShauN and Papi AQ on BODMON, the track that appears in the Northern Dial library.

Froboii is a Toronto-area hip-hop artist, songwriter and producer whose catalogue includes independent solo releases and collaborations within the city's current rap scene. His artist channels connect him directly with Toronto's 6ix-branded performance circuit and collaborators including Charmaine, JayTrillz and PHB Hollis. Northern Dial carries Froboii as part of its contemporary Toronto hip-hop catalogue.
Toronto-born Canadian producer Futurewave, born Martin Budik, is a leading underground boom-bap beatmaker known for rugged sampling and collaborations across independent hip-hop.

Quebec City-born, Montreal-based singer-songwriter Gabriella Olivo blends her Mexican and Québécois roots through French- and Spanish-language Latin electro-pop. Drawing on bolero, cumbia, indie music and cinematic textures, she has earned recognition including a 2025-26 Radio-Canada Révélation nod and ADISQ and GAMIQ nominations for her bilingual work.

Scarborough rapper Gangis Khan, also known as Camoflauge, is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose independent career grew out of Toronto's street-rap scene and collaborations across the city's rap community.
London, Ontario singer-songwriter Genevieve Fisher is a Canadian country artist with multiple national radio hits and repeated Country Music Association of Ontario award nominations.

Rohan White, who records as Ghostboyrj, was born in Toronto and raised in Brampton, where he began playing multiple instruments around age 12 before turning toward recording and production in his teens. Poetry and hip-hop became the bridge between those interests, and his involvement with Unity Charity helped deepen his understanding of hip-hop culture beyond simply making tracks. That grounding fed a style built around sample-driven production, boom-bap drums, jazz and soul textures and an emphasis on album-oriented underground rap.

Ghostboyrj's catalogue has developed through a steady independent release practice rather than a single commercial breakthrough. The 2021 project Elixir ++, made with producer Switch B and recorded in Toronto, established the collaborative, beat-focused direction of his work. Subsequent releases including just some beats, vol.1, Make Me Sick! and Remixology V2 have continued to blur the line between rapper and producer, while collaborations with artists such as The 6th Letter and Eyeda Sophia place him inside a wider network of Toronto-area independent hip-hop.

His importance is best understood at the scene level. Ghostboyrj represents a contemporary Brampton and Toronto underground that remains connected to older sample-based rap traditions while working through Bandcamp, home-studio production and direct independent releases. The value of the catalogue is not that it imitates a nostalgic boom-bap template, but that it keeps those production and writing methods active inside a younger GTA rap ecosystem that often receives less attention than the city's mainstream melodic and trap-oriented exports.

Glamboy is a Toronto hip-hop artist whose independent catalogue includes releases connected to the city's contemporary rap scene. His work has appeared alongside Toronto collaborators including 88GLAM, while solo material continues to develop his own artist identity. Northern Dial carries Glamboy as part of its Toronto hip-hop catalogue.
Toronto DJ, producer and composer Glenn Morrison is a Canadian electronic artist known for progressive house, melodic dance production and the international singles Contact and Goodbye.

GlomanOnThaBeat is a Toronto producer and recording artist whose independent catalogue spans hip-hop and beat-driven releases. He has collaborated with Canadian artists including Vancouver's Illyminiachi and has released projects such as Today and How 2. Northern Dial carries GlomanOnThaBeat as part of its Toronto hip-hop and producer catalogue.

Gnino is a Montreal rapper from Tétreaultville in the city's east end who grew up immersed in Quebec hip-hop through his father, rapper Rjboy. After beginning to write in his teens, he built momentum through the Cagoulé Gang duo and solo releases including Paranoia, developing a melodic, emotionally direct style within Montreal's francophone rap scene.

Formed in Langley, British Columbia, in the 1990s, Gob became one of the durable building blocks of Canadian punk before pop-punk became a major export category. Tom Thacker and Theo Goutzinakis shared guitar and vocal duties as the group developed a fast, melodic sound through early independent releases and the album Too Late... No Friends. How Far Shallow Takes You followed in 1998 and reached a wider North American audience, while years of touring and Warped Tour appearances gave Gob a reputation built as much on live momentum as radio play.

The World According to Gob arrived in 2001 and helped move the band further into the Canadian mainstream. The next major leap came with Foot in Mouth Disease in 2003, recorded with producer Mark Trombino after increased U.S. exposure through touring with Sum 41. Songs including "Give Up the Grudge" and "Oh! Ellin" sharpened the group's mix of punk speed and pop hooks, and a tour opening for Avril Lavigne placed Gob squarely inside the period when Canadian pop-punk was becoming an international commercial force.

Gob never depended on the same degree of crossover celebrity as Sum 41 or Simple Plan, which is part of why the band's role can be easy to understate. Its importance is more infrastructural: Gob was already building a Canadian audience, touring punk circuits and releasing melodic punk records before the genre's early-2000s boom. Thacker later joined Sum 41 as a touring and then full-time guitarist, creating another direct link between Canada's 1990s punk groundwork and the generation that carried the style onto a much larger global stage.

Golde London is a Toronto rapper from the Jane and Finch area whose music combines assertive street rap with melodic, personality-driven hooks. She has been active in Toronto's independent hip-hop scene through solo releases and collaborations with other Canadian women in rap. Her 2025 Think They Know Me remix with Haviah Mighty, Charmaine, TAAYLEE G and DvblM is her Northern Dial library credit.

Montréal singer, songwriter, musician and producer Grace of Arc makes alternative rock built around cinematic atmosphere, heavy dynamics and emotionally direct writing. Raised in a music-filled household and writing from a young age, Grace developed a style that pulls from rock, metal, opera, jazz and modern alternative pop rather than treating those influences as separate worlds.

The project began gaining wider attention with "Sides Of Me I’ve Never Met," which was selected as a SOCAN Song of the Week. Grace subsequently earned Spotify editorial support through playlists including ALT_QC and Fresh Finds Heavy, while 2026 singles such as "Rotten" and "La fin" continued sharpening the project’s dark, theatrical sound. Grace has also participated in artist-development programs including Canada’s Music Incubator and SOCAN Kenekt.

As a queer, non-binary artist of colour working in indie and alternative rock, Grace of Arc brings a perspective still underrepresented in those scenes. The project’s importance is not simply representational, though: the music is deliberately ambitious in its arrangement and production, making Grace part of a Montréal alternative ecosystem where genre, language and identity increasingly overlap.

Grand Eugène is a Montreal indie-rock and dream-pop project led by Melyssa Lemieux and Jeremy Lachance. The project began with songs developed between British Columbia and Quebec before taking shape in Montreal, and has grown through releases including its self-titled EP and Deux places au cimetière. Northern Dial carries Grand Eugène as part of Quebec's contemporary indie scene.
American-Canadian singer, songwriter and rapper grandson, born Jordan Benjamin, grew up in Toronto and blends alternative rock, hip-hop and electronic production with politically charged songwriting.

Gray Rowan is a Toronto producer and musician active across the city's R&B, electronic and independent music scenes. Rowan has co-produced work for artists including Maddee and contributed to recordings with Matthew Progress, Dan Only, Kingo Halla and Daniela Andrade, while also working from the NDG 208 studio in Toronto's east end. Northern Dial carries Gray Rowan as part of its Canadian producer and collaborator catalogue.

Great Big Sea formed in St. John's in 1993 and transformed Newfoundland traditional music into one of Canada's biggest folk-rock success stories. Alan Doyle, Séan McCann, Bob Hallett and early bassist Darrell Power drew on sea songs, dance tunes and material rooted in the island's Irish, English, Scottish and French traditions, but performed it with the energy and pacing of a touring rock band. The self-titled debut and 1995's Up built the foundation before Play became the national breakthrough in 1997.

Play included "Ordinary Day" and helped turn the band's communal live style into mainstream Canadian radio and arena success. Turn, Sea of No Cares and later releases continued balancing original songwriting with traditional repertoire, while relentless touring made Great Big Sea one of the country's defining live acts of the late 1990s and 2000s. The commercial scale was remarkable for music so closely tied to regional tradition: the band's studio catalogue repeatedly achieved gold and platinum certification in Canada.

Great Big Sea's significance is larger than folk-rock crossover. At a time when national pop success often encouraged artists to flatten regional identity, the band did the opposite, making Newfoundland language, repertoire and cultural references central to its mainstream appeal. The group retired after its 20th-anniversary period in 2013, but Doyle, McCann and Hallett's later work has kept parts of that catalogue active. Great Big Sea remains a key example of regional Canadian culture becoming national popular music without being stripped of place.

Scarborough rapper Grimace Love is a veteran of Toronto’s underground hip-hop scene and a longtime member of the Monolith collective. His solo work carries the rugged boom-bap sound associated with the crew while giving more room to his raspy delivery, storytelling and personal writing.
